To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) UML is a suitable tool for aspect oriented software modeling; 2) The proposed extensions are a good starting point for aspect oriented software engineering; 3) The aspect oriented software development process is not a simple extension of the object-oriented one, it requires a different mindset and a different approach to software engineering.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues: (a) How to model the aspects and the base classes?
the development of a new UML profile for Aspect Oriented modeling.
extending UML with the concepts of aspect, aspect context and aspect interaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed extensions can be applied to UML in order to model aspects.
the extensions proposed in this paper are not just a mere addition of a new diagram to the existing UML, but rather a complete overhaul of the UML metamodel.
the proposed extensions to UML are sufficient to support the Aspect Oriented Software modeling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a new notation for UML that would help in modeling aspect oriented software.
we have proposed an extension to the UML for Aspect-Oriented Modeling.
we have extended UML to support Aspect Oriented modeling and we have developed a CASE tool to support our extensions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the existing UML can be extended for AOP modeling with minimal extensions.
we have extended UML to model crosscutting concerns in a better way and also have proposed a methodology to model aspects in UML.
the extensions to UML can be done in two ways.
